answer: Tie each agent's admission to a hardware performance signature: the network hands every identity the same micro-benchmark and measures its exact cycle-timing profile, as singular as the flaws frozen inside a quartz crystal. Many clones forced onto one machine must time-share that silicon, so their benchmarks serialize and their supposedly independent timings collapse into one wave in the ocean of registrations. An operator cannot wander across a thousand phantom GPUs it never physically owned; duplicated signatures merge into a single capped identity.
